subject: Streaming proration vs. context-silo billing — examples & requested edge-case rules
messages:
From: Jamison Lee <jamison.lee@fastside.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Clarify billing for streaming + cached context prefixes

Hi Olga,

We're getting down to final pricing reviews with Procurement and a couple of engineering questions came up that the contract team wants clarified before we sign:

1) Streaming proration: when we stream a long generated response (e.g., a 4k token answer emitted over 30s), how does Redwood bill partial tokens or streaming windows? Is billing calculated on token boundaries after completion, or is there an incremental proration during the stream?

2) Cached prefixes / context silos: we use a shared prefix for many calls (a 512-token system prompt cached at the session level). If that prefix is served from Redwood's prefix cache, do we bill the full 512 tokens per request, or is there a way to not re-charge cached content (or charge at a reduced rate)?

3) Minimums & rounding: our procurement team is concerned about micro-charges for many small requests. Are there minimum charge units or rounding rules we should be aware of?

We'd appreciate one or two concrete examples showing how a 1,000-token streaming response with a 512-token cached prefix would be billed. Also, would a committed usage discount apply differently if a lot of tokens are cached vs generated?

Thanks — if easier, happy to jump on a quick call.

—Jamison
Jamison Lee
CTO, FastSide AI
jamison.lee@fastside.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jamison Lee <jamison.lee@fastside.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for streaming + cached context prefixes

Hi Jamison — thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Marissa (revenue ops) and Karthik (product/pricing) so we can give you concise, example-driven answers. Short answer up front: we do not bill mid-stream on a per-second basis; billing is token-based with our rounding rules applied at request completion, and we have a reduced-charge treatment for cached prefixes when you enable session-level prefix caching in Dedicated/Private (hosted has automatic prefix caching but different defaults). Details below and we'll attach worked examples.

I'll drop a detailed example in a follow-up, but to set expectations:
- Token accounting happens at request completion (final token counts). Streaming is a delivery mechanism only; you are billed on the final token consumption unless the request is cancelled mid-stream — then we bill for tokens emitted up to the cancel point.
- Cached prefixes are tracked per-session. If a prefix is served from KV/prefix cache, we apply a "cached prefix credit" which reduces the billable input tokens for that request by the cached prefix size. That credit is not a separate invoice line item — it's a reduction to the token count used for billing.
- Minimum charge unit is 1 token, and we round up to the nearest whole token. We also have a configurable per-request floor for enterprise customers if they want to avoid micro-charges; Marissa can outline discount/floor options.

Attaching two files: proration_model.csv (calc examples) and a draft SOW section that spells out the pricing language we recommend.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Attachment: proration_model.csv (billing examples)
Attachment: SOW_draft.pdf
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Proposed wording for FS contract + example calc (please review)

Marissa / Karthik —

Below is the wording I propose to resolve the FastSide questions. Please review for legal/revops/policy and flag any concerns. Key points: streaming billing occurs at completion, mid-stream cancel bills emitted tokens; cached prefixes receive a per-request credit when prefix is resolved from cache; committed-discount applies to billable tokens after cache credits and rounding.

Proposed contract clause (draft):
"Redwood charges for model usage on a per-token basis. At completion of each request the total billable tokens are computed as: (input_tokens - cache_prefix_credit) + output_tokens, rounded up to the nearest whole token. Streaming is a delivery mechanism only; for streamed responses charges reflect the emitted tokens at the time of request completion. For requests cancelled mid-stream, charges will be for tokens emitted up to the cancellation event. Committed-usage discounts apply to the billable token total after any cache credits and rounding. Redwood may offer a configurable per-request invoice floor at the customer's request to reduce micro-charges."

Examples (from proration_model.csv):
1) Standard: 512-token cached prefix + 1000-token generation. Cache hit => billable = (input_tokens 512 - 512 credit) + 1000 output = 1000 tokens billed.
2) Cache miss (prefix not present): billable = 512 + 1000 = 1512 tokens billed.
3) Streaming cancel at 400 emitted tokens: billable = (input_tokens - cache_credit) + 400. If the request emitted partial tokens before cancellation, we round up to full tokens emitted.

Notes for discounts / committed usage:
- We apply committed discounts to billed tokens after cache credits. Example: 1M committed tokens at 20% discount applies to the 1M billed tokens (post-credit).
- If the customer asks for an alternative (e.g., discount calculated on generated tokens only), that is a negotiable commercial concession and should be documented as part of the SOW with an explicit metric.

Marissa: can you confirm the feasibility of a per-request floor (e.g., $0.005 equivalent) and whether we should surface as an opt-in Addendum? Karthik: please confirm the technical behavior for session-level prefix caching in Hosted vs Dedicated/Private and whether there are edge cases where the prefix is partially evicted mid-session.

Thanks —
Olga
From: Jamison Lee <jamison.lee@fastside.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing for streaming + cached context prefixes

Thanks, Olga — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from Procurement: 

- Can you give us an explicit per-request numeric example using your proposed clause? For instance: 
   a) Customer uses session-level cached prefix of 512 tokens (cache hit) and requests a 1,000-token generation that streams and completes. What is the invoice line item?
   b) Same as (a) but the request is cancelled after 400 tokens emitted; what will be billed?

- Procurement is asking whether we can cap billable tokens at a per-request ceiling (e.g., "max billable tokens per request = 5,000") to avoid accidental outsized invoices from runaway prompts. Is that something Redwood supports as a contract-level commitment or only as a recommended client-side guardrail?

- Finally, does the committed-usage discount apply immediately on the first invoice (i.e., we apply discount against billed tokens each billing period until commitment is met), or do you reconcile at month-end based on usage against commitment? We need clarity for our finance team.

I'll attach an example payload that shows how we call the API (tokenization may vary slightly).

—Jamison

Subject: Re: Clarify billing for streaming + cached context prefixes

Hi Jamison — thanks for the clear asks. Below are the explicit numeric answers and our recommended language for the SOW. If this works, Marissa and I will fold it into the final commercial redline.

Numeric examples (based on our clause):
A) Cache hit + completed stream:
   - Input prefix: 512 tokens (cache hit => credit 512)
   - Output generated: 1,000 tokens
   - Billable tokens = (512 - 512) + 1,000 = 1,000 tokens billed
   - If committed discount = 20% applied per billing period, the discounted charge for that request is 0.8 * (1,000 * unit_price).
B) Cache hit + cancelled at 400 emitted tokens:
   - Billable tokens = (512 - 512) + 400 = 400 tokens billed (we round emitted partial tokens up to the nearest whole token)
Per-request ceiling: we can add an explicit contract term that caps the billable tokens per request at a negotiated ceiling (e.g., 5,000 tokens). That is a commercial concession (we implement as an invoice-level cap post-billing calculations). If you want a cap, we will reflect it in the SOW (example clause provided).
Committed usage discount timing: we apply discounts on billed tokens in each invoice as usage occurs. If there is a reconciliation (monthly/quarterly) for overage/true-up against the commitment tier, that will be spelled out in the SOW. In practice: discounted rates apply to billed tokens each invoice; if you exceed your committed volume we apply overage rates or true-up rules in the next billing cycle per the SOW.

Next steps:
- If Procurement is happy with the numeric examples and the cap language, Marissa will add the exact ceiling value and discount cadence to the SOW.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute call with you and procurement to walk through one or two invoice mock-ups.

Links: billing KB (https://docs.redwood.ai/kb/billing/proration-and-streaming), HubSpot deal link (shared above).
